summary: GCP->AWS assume-role path blocked by IAM condition on ops-service-account, breaking cluster diagnostic tooling
description:
Issue summary: Scheduled diagnostics and live debugging from the SRE toolkit fail when attempting to impersonate the GCP ops-service-account and then assume the linked AWS cross-account role. The failure appears to be caused by an IAM Condition on the GCP side that blocks token exchange when a specific session tag is present.

Impact: SRE runbook executions that require cross-cloud debugging are blocked for multiple platform teams. This prevents live investigation of high-latency incidents in Dedicated clusters and delays incident response. Affects internal tooling and some on-call escalations.

Environment: prod | us-east (GCP), prod | us-east-1 (AWS). Affected clusters: redwood-dedicated-prod-us-east-01 and redwood-debug-proxy-prod.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From an SRE workstation with normal SSO session, run the ops-tooling script that calls gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate for projects/infra/ops-service-account
2) Attempt to exchange the impersonated credentials to assume-role in the AWS debug account via our broker (sts:AssumeRole with external ID)
3) Observe failure immediately with a 403 on the token-exchange and a subsequent AssumeRoleDenied error in the AWS broker logs.
logs:
GCP IAM debug: 'Token exchange denied: condition request.auth.claims.session_tag != "ops-debug"'
Broker log (aws-broker-prod): AssumeRoleDenied - sts:AssumeRole - role arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/redwood-debug-role - reason: invalid token
Ops-tooling stdout: 'Impersonation succeeded locally; token exchange failed: 403 Forbidden'.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: recent org-level IAM Condition introduced to restrict service-account impersonation when a session tag is present. Verified via gcloud iam policies that a conditional binding exists on infra/ops-service-account restricting iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken when request.auth.claims.session_tag == "ops-debug".
Checked SSO token payloads and found session_tag populated by the new session middleware we rolled out last week (INT-472999 referenced).
Reproduced with a synthetic service account token: tokens without session_tag exchange successfully; tokens with session_tag are rejected.
AWS side: broker expects a standard OAuth token; it rejects tokens that have non-standard claims. The broker logs show token validation failed rather than role trust policy rejecting the role; suggests upstream token was invalid when presented to STS proxy.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Priya Nambiar: Implemented temporary token filter in ops-tooling to strip session_tag before exchange; verified cross-account assume runs succeed in canary cluster. Need permanent fix.

2026-03-14 10:10 - Marco Ruiz: Proposed long-term fixes: (A) adjust IAM Condition expression to whitelist the SRE impersonation path, (B) update broker to accept tokens with session_tag after validating origin, or (C) add a dedicated service account without the conditional binding for cross-cloud ops. Security prefers A with constrained whitelist.
2026-03-14 12:05 - Priya Nambiar: Noted follow-up: define smallest-privilege condition and rollout plan; coordinate with Security and Platform to avoid re-openings.
next_steps:
1) Implement IAM Condition whitelist for projects/infra/ops-service-account limited to serviceAccount:roles/sre-debug and audit binding (Security to approve).
2) Add integration test in auth-broker suite that validates token exchange with session_tag present.
3) Patch broker to log token origin and provide clearer error codes for token validation failures.
4) Schedule follow-up change window and notify oncall.
Owners: Marco (Auth Eng) for condition change, Priya (SRE) for broker tests and ops-tooling patch.
